title: refactor(ci): simplify lint/test/release workflows and bump GH Actions/deps
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: Over the last year our repo accumulated multiple overlapping GitHub Actions workflows: separate lint/test release pipelines in .github/workflows that duplicated logic, inconsistent Node versions, and a growing list of action pin/version drift. This caused longer CI runtime, inconsistent cache behavior, and occasional flaky releases.

This PR consolidates lint, unit/integration test, and release automation workflows into a smaller set of standardized, reusable workflows and a single CI helper script. Goals: reduce runtime by avoiding duplicated setup steps, improve cache hit-rate across jobs, standardize Node/action versions, and make release automation easier to maintain.

What I changed:
- Introduced consolidated workflows: .github/workflows/lint.yml, .github/workflows/test.yml, .github/workflows/release.yml (replacing four older workflow files).
- Centralized common steps in scripts/ci/common.sh and a small actions/README for maintainers.
- Bumped GH Action versions and standard tooling: actions/checkout@v4, actions/setup-node@v4, actions/cache@v4, pnpm/action-setup@v2.
- Standardized Node runtime to 20.x for CI, with a small matrix for 18 and 20 only on the core redwood packages to keep compatibility testing.
- Improved caching strategy: use composite cache keys for pnpm store and test deps, and restored correct cache paths to improve hit-rate across matrix jobs.
- Fixed flaky fs-related test by ensuring test runner uses --runInBand under constrained matrix shards.
- Simplified release automation: using release-please-config with a single release.yml that supports canary/candidate/stable flows and uploads artifacts for debugging failed releases.
- Dependency hygiene: bumped devDependencies in root package.json (eslint, jest, pnpm) and updated a couple of internal CI helper packages.

Notes:
- Kept separate small workflows for perf-canary and perf-canary-release because they have long-running steps and should not block PR CI.
- Left a short migration guide in actions/README for teams that still need bespoke steps.

Backwards compatibility: The changes are additive for developers; existing PRs will run using the new consolidated pipelines. The release automation behavior is kept feature-parity but more observable (artifact upload + explicit release logs).

Testing performed: ran the consolidated workflows on this branch (see CI runs below), validated cache hits on subsequent reruns, and executed local smoke tests for release-please flows against a sandbox repo.

Related: ENG-7821 tracks follow-up work to extract common action steps into a reusable composite action.
